chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who attained an ostrich egg while he was in Ihram. He said: 'He should send a male camel for each egg.' I said: 'What if the eggs spoil entirely, or remain good entirely?' He said: 'Whatever is produced from the sacrificial animal is the sacrifice reaching the Kaaba; and if it is not produced, there is nothing upon him.' So whoever cannot find a camel, upon him is a sheep for each egg. If he cannot find one, then charity upon ten poor people, for each poor person a Mudd. If he is not able, then fasting for three days.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific measure of volume for food (approx. 750g)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for catching an ostrich egg while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the graduated expiation (kaffarah) for catching wild game while in Ihram, using the ostrich egg as a specific case study to illustrate the principle of proportional compensation. It reflects the Shia juristic methodology of determining value through the 'fahl' (male camel) and provides a clear hierarchy of remedies—camels, sheep, feeding the poor, and fasting—ensuring accessibility for those with varying means. The ruling underscores the spiritual seriousness of violating Ihram restrictions while offering practical flexibility based on economic capacity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who attained an egg of an ostrich, and he was in Ihraam. Heasws said: ‘He should send (as a sacrifice), the stallion among the camels upon the number of the eggs’.  I said, ‘Supposing the eggs get spoilt, all of them, and (if) they are correct, all of them’. Heasws said: ‘What is befitting from the sacrifice, so it is the sacrifice reaching the Kabah; and if it produces, so there is nothing upon him. So the one who cannot find a camel, so upon him, for each of the eggs, is a sheep. So if he cannot find, so let him give in charity upon ten poor ones, for each poor one being a Mudd (750 gms.). So if he is not able, so he should Fast for three days’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is involved in hunting matters of the egg of ostrich while in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must send male camel on female camel equal to the number of eggs affected.’ I then said, ‘Eggs may all become spoiled or all of them may hatch.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever the product is, as offering it must reach al- Ka‘bah; and if there is no product one does not owe anything. If one cannot find camels, then for every egg he must pay one sheep; and if one cannot find this also, then one must give charity to ten destitute people, one mud (a certain measurement) to each one and if one cannot afford this also then must fast three days.’”
